title: How to manage a social media manager contract on Mac for professional growth
metaTitle: Social media manager contract management: tips for Mac users
description: Learn to handle your social media manager contract on Mac to stop scope creep, prevent burnout, and ensure you get paid for every hour worked.
secondaryKeywords: Mac productivity for social media managers
intro: A solid social media manager contract is the primary defense against scope creep and unpaid overtime. Without clear terms on your Mac, you risk working hours that are never billed, leading to the burnout that affects many in this field.
tldr: Define exact deliverables in your contract to stop scope creep.
Use a centralized platform on your Mac to track contracts and invoices.
Set clear boundaries for communication and response times.
Include specific clauses for revisions and additional project requests.

blocks.text: Why your social media manager contract matters

Many social media managers start with informal agreements. This is a mistake. When you do not define the work, the work defines you. Clients often assume that social media management includes everything from graphic design to crisis management and ad buying. If these are not in your contract, you are likely doing them for free.

items: Vague scope of work: Using terms like 'manage social media' instead of listing specific platforms and post counts.
Lack of revision limits: Allowing unlimited edits to designs or captions in Canva.
Undefined working hours: No clear statement on when you are available for urgent requests.
Fragmented documentation: Keeping contracts in one folder, invoices in another, and emails elsewhere.

blocks.text: You do not need expensive software to fix these issues. Start by auditing your current workflow on your Mac. Open your Finder and create a dedicated folder for each client. Use a consistent naming convention like YYYY-MM-DD-ClientName-Contract. This simple step stops you from hunting for documents when a dispute arises.
If you are a contractor, always include a clause that defines the maximum number of revisions per post. This prevents endless back-and-forth in Slack or email.
blocks.title: Set Revision Limits

blocks.text: When a client asks for extra work, refer them to the contract. You can say: 'I would be happy to add that to our scope. Let me draft a quick amendment for that specific task.' This keeps the relationship professional and ensures you are paid for your time.

faq.question: What should I include in a social media manager contract?
faq.answer: Include a detailed list of deliverables, revision counts, payment schedules, intellectual property rights, and termination notice periods.

faq.question: How do I deal with clients who ask for more work?
faq.answer: Politely acknowledge the request, check your contract, and propose a change order if the work falls outside the original agreement.
